Jesus Is Lord of the Sabbath
1 One Sabbath Jesus was going through the grainfields, and his disciples began to pick some heads of grain, rub them in their hands and eat the kernels. 2 Some of the Pharisees asked, “Why are you doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath?”

3 Jesus answered them, “Have you never read what David did when he and his companions were hungry? 4 He entered the house of God, and taking the consecrated bread, he ate what is lawful only for priests to eat. And he also gave some to his companions.” 5 Then Jesus said to them, “The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”

1 On another Sabbath he went into the synagogue and was teaching, and a man was there whose right hand was shriveled. 7 The Pharisees and the teachers of the law were looking for a reason to accuse Jesus, so they watched him closely to see if he would heal on the Sabbath. 8 But Jesus knew what they were thinking and said to the man with the shriveled hand, “Get up and stand in front of everyone.” So he got up and stood there.

9 Then Jesus said to them, “I ask you, which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?”

10 He looked around at them all, and then said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He did so, and his hand was completely restored. 11 But the Pharisees and the teachers of the law were furious and began to discuss with one another what they might do to Jesus.

The Twelve Apostles
12 One of those days Jesus went out to a mountainside to pray, and spent the night praying to God. 13 When morning came, he called his disciples to him and chose twelve of them, whom he also designated apostles: 14 Simon (whom he named Peter), his brother Andrew, James, John, Philip, Bartholomew, 15 Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Simon who was called the Zealot, 16 Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.

Blessings and Woes
17 He went down with them and stood on a level place. A large crowd of his disciples was there and a great number of people from all over Judea, from Jerusalem, and from the coastal region around Tyre and Sidon, 18 who had come to hear him and to be healed of their diseases. Those troubled by impure spirits were cured, 19 and the people all tried to touch him, because power was coming from him and healing them all.

20 Looking at his disciples, he said:

“Blessed are you who are poor,
for yours is the kingdom of God.
21 Blessed are you who hunger now,
for you will be satisfied.
Blessed are you who weep now,
for you will laugh.
22 Blessed are you when people hate you,
when they exclude you and insult you
and reject your name as evil,
because of the Son of Man.

23 “Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, because great is your reward in heaven. For that is how their ancestors treated the prophets.

24 “But woe to you who are rich,
for you have already received your comfort.
25 Woe to you who are well fed now,
for you will go hungry.
Woe to you who laugh now,
for you will mourn and weep.
26 Woe to you when everyone speaks well of you,
for that is how their ancestors treated the false prophets.

Love for Enemies
27 “But to you who are listening I say: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, 28 bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you. 29 If someone slaps you on one cheek, turn to them the other also. If someone takes your coat, do not withhold your shirt from them. 30 Give to everyone who asks you, and if anyone takes what belongs to you, do not demand it back. 31 Do to others as you would have them do to you.

32 “If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love those who love them. 33 And if you do good to those who are good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do that. 34 And if you lend to those from whom you expect repayment, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, expecting to be repaid in full. 35 But love your enemies, do good to them, and lend to them without expecting to get anything back. Then your reward will be great, and you will be children of the Most High, because he is kind to the ungrateful and wicked. 36 Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.

Judging Others
37 “Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven. 38 Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together and running over, will be poured into your lap. For with the measure you use, it will be measured to you.”

39 He also told them this parable: “Can the blind lead the blind? Will they not both fall into a pit? 40 The student is not above the teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like their teacher.

41 “Why do you look at the speck of sawdust in your brother’s eye and pay no attention to the plank in your own eye? 42 How can you say to your brother, ‘Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,’ when you yourself fail to see the plank in your own eye? You hypocrite, first take the plank out of your eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.

A Tree and Its Fruit
43 “No good tree bears bad fruit, nor does a bad tree bear good fruit. 44 Each tree is recognized by its own fruit. People do not pick figs from thornbushes, or grapes from briers. 45 A good man brings good things out of the good stored up in his heart, and an evil man brings evil things out of the evil stored up in his heart. For the mouth speaks what the heart is full of.

The Wise and Foolish Builders
46 “Why do you call me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ and do not do what I say? 47 As for everyone who comes to me and hears my words and puts them into practice, I will show you what they are like. 48 They are like a man building a house, who dug down deep and laid the foundation on rock. When a flood came, the torrent struck that house but could not shake it, because it was well built. 49 But the one who hears my words and does not put them into practice is like a man who built a house on the ground without a foundation. The moment the torrent struck that house, it collapsed and its destruction was complete.”
translations:
耶稣是安息日的主
1 有一天安息日,耶稣经过谷田,门徒们了小麦,把它们在手里,吃了. 2 有法利赛人问他们:"你们为什么在安息日行违禁的呢?"

3 耶稣回答说:大卫和他同伴饥饿的时候,你们没有读过大卫所做的吗? 4 他进了神的殿,拿了献给神的饼,吃了,除了祭司以外,没有法可以吃的,还给了他同行的. 5 耶稣又对他们说:人子是安息日的主.

1 又有一天安息日,耶稣进了犹太教堂,就教训.那里有一个手的男人. 7 法利赛人和律法学家,就着耶稣,看他是否在安息日治愈,以找理由指控他. 8 耶稣知道他们的心思,对那手的人说: "起来,站在中间. "他就起来站了.

9 耶稣对他们说:我问你们,安息日可以做好事还是做恶,救命还是灭亡?

10 他环顾他们,然后对那人说:伸出你的手.他就这样做,他的手就完全好了. 11 他们的心就然,他们就彼此商议,要怎样行耶稣.
12 有一天,耶稣上山祷告,一夜祷告上帝. 13 到了早晨,他召了门徒来,拣选了十二个人,并称他们为使徒. 14 希门 (他又给他起了彼得),他的兄弟安德烈,雅各,约翰,腓力,巴多利米, 15 马太福音,托马斯,阿尔弗叶的儿子雅各,西门,称为子, 16 雅各的儿子犹大,和卖卖的犹大斯加略特.
17 耶稣和门徒下来,站在平原的地方.他的门徒的许多人,还有许多人从全犹大,耶路撒冷,西顿和罗边境, 18 他们来听耶稣说话,被医治他们的病.被污秽的灵困扰的人也被医治. 19 众人都试图摸着耶稣,因为从他里出来的力量都治愈了他们.

20 耶稣着眼睛看着门徒说:你们穷人,有福了,因为神的国是你们的.
21 你们现在饥饿的人,有福了,因为你们必满足.你们现在哭泣的人,有福了,因为你们必笑.
22 当人恨你们,因为人子,把你们排斥,谤,弃你们的名的时候,你们是有福的.

23 那天,你们要欢喜,欢喜大大,因为你们在天上将得重大的报酬.他们的祖先也这样待了先知.

24 但有祸了,你们富人,因为你们已经得到了你们的安慰.
25 你们现在吃得够的,有祸了,因为你们必饿了.你们现在笑的人,有祸了,因为你们要哀哭哭.
26 人人都赞美你们,有祸了!他们的祖先也这样对假先知说话.爱敌人,
27 现在,我告诉你们听我的话,要爱你们的敌人,要行善你们的仇敌. 28 你们要祝福那些咒诅你们的人,为迫害你们的人祈祷. 29 谁打你的脸,就把另一面也转给他.谁拿你的子,就不要住你的衫. 30 凡要求你的人,就给他;凡夺走你的东西的人,就不要要求他回来. 31 你们要怎样待别人,你们也要怎样待别人.

32 你们若爱爱爱你们的,有甚麽荣誉呢?罪人也爱爱爱爱爱他们的. 33 你们若向你们行善的人行善,你们有甚麽荣誉呢?罪人也这样行. 34 你们若借给那些希望还给的人,那你们有什么荣誉呢?罪人也借给罪人,希望还给他们. 35 你们要爱你们的仇敌,善待他们,借贷他们,不要期待收回什么.那么,你们的报酬将是大大的,你们就成为至高者的子孙,因为他对不感谢和不义的人是仁慈的. 36 你们要怜悯,如你们的父怜悯.
37 不要审判,你们也不被审判;不要谴责,你们也不被谴责;要宽恕,你们也必蒙宽恕. 38 你们要施舍,你们就必得.你们要拿着的,的,的,的,好的量,将倒在你们的怀里.因为你们用那量度,就用那量度,就会给你们.

39 耶稣又对他们说了这比喻:"瞎子能领瞎子去吗?他们俩都不会掉进坑里吗? 40 学生不过老师,但凡经过训练的都就像老师.

41 你为什么看着弟兄眼中的子,却不注意你自己的眼中的子呢? 42 你怎能对你的弟兄说:弟兄,让我把那块从你的眼睛里拿出来,而你自己看不到自己的眼中的子呢?伪君啊,先把那块从你的眼睛里拿出来,然后你就能清楚地看见,把那块从你弟兄的眼睛里拿出来.树和果子.
43 好树不能生坏果子,坏树也不能生良好的果子. 44 因为各树因自己的果子而认识.人们不从棘中摘果,也不是从树中摘葡萄. 45 好人从心里积蓄的善中,拿出善,恶人从心里积蓄的恶中拿出恶.心里充满的口就说出.智慧人和愚昧的人,都是建造的人.
46 你们为什么叫我说主,主,却不遵行我的话呢? 47 凡来到我这里,听我的话,遵行我的话,我告诉你们,他是怎样的人. 48 他们就像一个人建造房子,深挖,在磐石上奠定基础.洪水涌来,冲击了房子,但不能动摇,因为房子是好建造的. 49 惟有听见不遵行的人,就像一个人,在地上建造房屋,没有基石.那房子一旦洪水涌来,就倒塌了,其毁灭就甚了.
